In 10, a harvest count at Meigate revealed a grain shortage that caused a famine killing twenty-three people. Eight years later, in 18, old grudges cooled and the standing of the Kebarrow Compact eroded, leading to the beating off of its raid on Vea Lode. The following year, Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact to become the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 20, Weallhous Dreld challenged Krir Nur for the leadership of the Kebarrow Compact and took the seat, casting out the losing side. Consequently, Laehiford also broke from the Kebarrow Compact to form the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

Two years later, in 22, Saern Meastouth won Paernrom Sir away from the ruler of the Kebarrow Compact, and two years after that, in 24, Paernrom Sir won Paernmel Has away from the same ruler. In 25, Gatros Hearn challenged Weallhous Dreld for the leadership of the Kebarrow Compact and took the seat through a coup. Four years later, in 29, Wilwound Ska murdered Theald Va at Hadale, killing the ruler of the Kebarrow Compact. Wilwound then contested Beas Krouthea’s claim to the leadership under the rule of election, resulting in Beas being cast out as the losing claimant.

In 30, Beas returned from exile and took service with the Vea Lode Covenant. Five years later, in 35, he began conspiring against Stald Gearngoll of that power. After one year, his conspiracy was uncovered in 36, leading to his casting out for plotting against the seat. Four years after that, in 40, Beas returned from exile once more and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate.

In 10, a harvest count at Meigate preceded a famine that killed 23 people and left grain short by one unit. Eight years later, in 18, old grudges cooled as standing quietly eroded, leading to the Kebarrow Compact’s raid on Vea Lode being beaten off in 19. The following year, Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact to become the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 20, Laehiford broke from the Kebarrow Compact to become the Sworn Men of Laehiford because of Krir Nur’s exile. Two years later, Saern Meastouth won Paernrom Sir away from the ruler of the Kebarrow Compact, and two years after that, Paernrom Sir won Paernmel Has away from the same ruler. In 25, Gatros Hearn challenged Weallhous Dreld openly for the Kebarrow Compact and took the seat, establishing his rule through a coup in 25. Four years later, Wilwound Ska had Theald Va murdered at Hadale, leading to Theald Va’s death by Wilwound Ska at Hadale in 29.

In 29, Wilwound Ska contested Beas Krouthea’s claim to the Kebarrow Compact under election rules, resulting in Beas Krouthea being cast out as the losing claimant. One year later, Beas Krouthea returned from exile and took service with the Vea Lode Covenant. Six years after that, in 36, an unattributed attempt on Stald Gearngoll failed at Vea Lode, a consequence of Beas Krouthea’s prior alignment with the Covenant.

In 19, Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact to form the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 20, Sou Dra returned from exile and took service with the group. That same year, the Sworn Men raided Laehiford, carrying off 39 grain and killing 22. In 22, Sou Dra challenged Renbeir Surn openly for the seat and was beaten. Sou Dra was cast out as the losing side of a coup. In 23, the Sworn Men raided Hadale, carrying off 33 grain and killing 12. In 25, Renbeir Surn died. Kreathbeas Waeth took the seat after being raised from Meigate with no remaining claimant.

In 26, a famine at Meigate left 64 dead and grain short by 7. In 28, Krir Nur and Gatros Hearn returned from exile to take service. The Sworn Men’s raids on Griwick, Vea Lode, and Threi Cut were beaten off in 28 and 29. In 31, Tor Nathgoull returned from exile. In 40, Beas Krouthea and Herpeim Raern returned from exile. In 41, Gatros Hearn’s attempt on Kreathbeas Waeth failed and was traced back. He was cast out for attempted murder. His conspiracy against Kreathbeas Waeth was uncovered after two years, leading to his second casting out for conspiracy against the seat.

In 42, a famine killed 75 and left grain short by 8. Raids on Griwick and Vea Lode were beaten off. In 43, a second year of famine killed 47 and caused 238 to abandon Meigate. A raid on Threi Cut was beaten off. The Vea Lode Covenant raided Meigate, killing 22. In 47, Treild Haen married Stoulthoth Frorn, binding the Sworn Men to the Sworn Men of Laehiford. In 48, Kreathbeas Waeth died. Stonand Ker and Throll Kell returned from exile. Herpeim Raern took the seat by election. In 50, Treild Haen challenged Herpeim Raern openly and took the seat. Herpeim Raern was cast out as the losing side of a coup. In 51, Treild Haen’s attempt on Viskeil Von failed. He was cast out for attempted murder. Beas Krouthea took the seat by election.

In 19, Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact to form the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 20, Sou Dra returned from exile and took service with the new power. That same year, the Sworn Men raided Laehiford, carrying off 39 grain and killing 22. In 22, Sou Dra challenged Renbeir Surn openly for the seat of the Sworn Men of Meigate and was beaten. Sou Dra was cast out of the Sworn Men of Meigate as the losing side of a coup.

Renbeir Surn, ruler of the Sworn Men of Meigate, died in 25 at Meigate. Kreathbeas Waeth took the seat of the Sworn Men of Meigate in 25, raised from Meigate with no claimant remaining. A famine struck Meigate in 26, leaving 64 dead and grain short by 7. In 28, Krir Nur and Gatros Hearn returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate. That year, the Sworn Men’s raids on Griwick, Vea Lode, and Threi Cut were all beaten off.

Tor Nathgoull returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate in 31. In 40, Beas Krouthea and Herpeim Raern returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 41, Gatros Hearn’s attempt on Kreathbeas Waeth failed and was traced back. Gatros Hearn was cast out of the Sworn Men of Meigate for attempted murder. His conspiracy against Kreathbeas Waeth was uncovered after two years, and he was cast out again for conspiracy against the seat. Kondruth Tru returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate in 41.

A famine at Meigate in 42 left 75 dead and grain short by 8. The Sworn Men’s raids on Griwick and Vea Lode were beaten off in 42. A second year of famine in 43 killed 47 and caused 238 to abandon Meigate. The Sworn Men’s raid on Threi Cut was beaten off in 43. The Vea Lode Covenant raided Meigate in 43, killing 22. In 47, Treild Haen married Stoulthoth Frorn, binding the Sworn Men of Meigate to the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

Kreathbeas Waeth, ruler of the Sworn Men of Meigate, died in 48 at Meigate. Stonand Ker and Throll Kell returned from exile and took service with the Sworn Men of Meigate in 48. Herpeim Raern took the seat of the Sworn Men of Meigate by election in 48. In 50, Treild Haen challenged Herpeim Raern openly for the seat and took it. Treild Haen took the seat of the Sworn Men of Meigate by coup. Herpeim Raern was cast out of the Sworn Men of Meigate as the losing side of a coup.

In 51, Treild Haen’s attempt on Viskeil Von failed and was traced back. Treild Haen was cast out of the Sworn Men of Meigate for attempted murder. Beas Krouthea took the seat of the Sworn Men of Meigate by election in 51.

The Sworn Men of Meigate existed for thirty-three years, from 19 to 51, as a power that began by breaking from the Kebarrow Compact and ended by losing its seat to the Vea Lode Covenant. Its rule passed through three holders, each serving an average of ten years, before the house ended. The period was defined by internal instability, marked by open challenges and conspiracies, and by external failure, as most raids were beaten off and the power was eventually destroyed.

Renbeir Surn took the seat in 19 when Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact. He faced an open challenge from Sou Dra in 22, which Renbeir won, but Sou Dra was cast out. Renbeir died in 25, and Kreathbeas Waeth took the seat. Under Kreathbeas, the Sworn Men sent eight raids against the Griwick Compact and the Vea Lode Covenant. Two raids on Laehiford and Hadale carried off plunder, but six raids on Griwick, Vea Lode, and Threi Cut were beaten off. Gatros Hearn attempted to murder Kreathbeas in 41 and was cast out, later declared outlaw for conspiracy.

The power declined through famine and war. Three years of hunger killed 186 people. In 43, the Vea Lode Covenant raided Meigate. In 48, Kreathbeas died, and Tor Nathgoull took the seat after Herpeim Raern’s claim was set aside. The Vea Lode Covenant declared war in 49. Tor Nathgoull had Keithfal Naell murdered in 50, but the Vea Lode Covenant took Meigate that same year. The Sworn Men of Meigate was finished, its last 12 followers scattering. Peace was made in 51.

The Sworn Men of Meigate existed for thirty-three years, from 19 to 51, as a power that began by breaking from the Kebarrow Compact and ended by losing its seat to the Vea Lode Covenant. The period was defined by internal instability, repeated military failure, and a final collapse. Three people held the seat: Renbeir Surn, Kreathbeas Waeth, and Tor Nathgoull. Their rules lasted an average of 10.3 years, with a median of 6.0 years. The seat passed from one person to another two times inside this period.

Renbeir Surn took the seat in 19 when Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact. He faced an open challenge from Sou Dra in 22, which he won, but Sou Dra was cast out. Renbeir died in 25, and Kreathbeas Waeth took the seat. Under Kreathbeas, the Sworn Men sent eight raids. Two carried off plunder: Laehiford in 20 and Hadale in 23. Six were beaten off: Griwick in 28, Vea Lode in 28, Threi Cut in 29, Griwick in 42, Vea Lode in 42, and Threi Cut in 43. The power suffered one raid, by the Vea Lode Covenant at Meigate in 43.

Internal strife continued under Kreathbeas. Gatros Hearn attempted murder in 41 and was cast out, then declared outlaw for conspiracy. Three people were cast out in total: one for attempted murder, one for the losing claim, and one for the losing side of an open challenge. Eight exiles returned to service. The power endured three years of hunger or sickness, killing 186 in all. In 48, Kreathbeas died. Tor Nathgoull took the seat after setting aside Herpeim Raern’s claim. Tor Nathgoull had Keithfal Naell murdered at Vea Lode in 50. The Vea Lode Covenant took Meigate from the Sworn Men in 50. The Sworn Men were finished, landless, with its last 12 followers scattering. The Vea Lode Covenant and the Sworn Men made peace in 51 after two years of war.

The Vea Lode Covenant entered the period as a power defined by electoral succession and active expansion. Its standing was bolstered by the return of Herpeim Raern, who took service with the Covenant in year 49. The Covenant’s posture was aggressive, initiating a war against the Sworn Men of Meigate over a long-standing grievance. This conflict defined the early years, leading to decisive victories that altered the regional balance of power.

In year 49, the Covenant defeated the Sworn Men of Meigate at Meigate, killing 149 men. The war continued into year 50, where the Covenant secured another victory at the same site, resulting in 124 deaths. These defeats allowed the Covenant to take Meigate from the Sworn Men. The Sworn Men of Meigate was finished, becoming landless with its last 12 followers scattering. The Covenant and the Sworn Men of Meigate made peace in year 51, ending the two-year conflict.

The period ended with the collapse of the Covenant’s authority. In year 50, Keithfal Naell, the ruler of the Vea Lode Covenant, was killed by Tor Nathgoull at Vea Lode. Herpeim Raern took the seat of the Covenant by election following this death. Despite this succession, the Covenant’s standing had fallen to nothing. In year 51, Threi Cut rose against the Vea Lode Covenant. The power that had begun the period with military victories and a new ruler ended it facing internal rebellion and lost influence.

The Vea Lode Covenant entered the period as a power engaged in a war of conquest, emerging from it diminished by internal violence and external rebellion. At the start, the Covenant held the initiative against the Sworn Men of Meigate, a conflict driven by a long-standing grievance. Herpeim Raern returned from exile to serve the Covenant, while its ruler, Keithfal Naell, directed military operations that resulted in the destruction of its enemy.

The Covenant’s fortunes shifted with the death of its ruler. In year 50, Keithfal Naell was killed at Vea Lode by Tor Nathgoull. Herpeim Raern took the seat by election in the same year. Although the Covenant had already defeated the Sworn Men of Meigate at Meigate and taken the settlement, the power of its enemy collapsed completely, leaving its last twelve followers scattered. The Covenant and the Sworn Men of Meigate made peace after two years, following the enemy's dissolution.

By year 51, the Covenant’s standing had fallen to nothing. Threi Cut rose against the Covenant, exploiting this weakness. Earlier in the year, a raid by the Hadale Commune on Meigate was beaten off, but the Covenant could no longer maintain its authority. The period ended with the Covenant’s power broken by the rebellion at Threi Cut, a direct consequence of the vacuum left by the ruler’s death.

The Vea Lode Covenant entered the period as a power engaged in a war of conquest, emerging from it with its seat secured by election but its territorial gains and internal stability shattered. The conflict with the Sworn Men of Meigate defined the early years, resulting in decisive victories for the Covenant and the total destruction of its enemy. However, the assassination of the ruler Keithfal Naell in year 50 triggered a collapse in the Covenant’s standing, allowing a rebellion at Threi Cut to rise against it by the end of the period.

In year 49, the Covenant declared war on the Sworn Men of Meigate over a long-standing grievance. This campaign yielded immediate results: the Covenant defeated the Sworn Men at Meigate in year 49, killing 149 men, and again in year 50, killing 124. Following the second victory, the Covenant took Meigate from the Sworn Men. The Sworn Men of Meigate was finished that same year, becoming landless as its last 12 followers scattered. The Covenant and the Sworn Men made peace in year 51, two years after the collapse of the Sworn Men.

The internal stability of the Covenant fractured in year 50 when Keithfal Naell, the ruler, was killed by Tor Nathgoull at Vea Lode. Herpeim Raern took the seat of the Vea Lode Covenant by election in year 50 following this death. Despite the new ruler, the Covenant’s standing had fallen to nothing by year 51. In that year, Threi Cut rose against the Covenant. The Hadale Commune also attempted a raid on Meigate in year 51, but it was beaten off.

The Vea Lode Covenant entered the period as a power defined by its succession by election and its control of Vea Lode. Its standing was high enough to declare war, yet fragile enough that the death of its ruler could unravel its authority. The period began with the return of Herpeim Raern, who took service with the Covenant after exile, and ended with the site of Threi Cut rising against it as its standing had fallen to nothing. The Covenant’s trajectory was shaped by a war against the Sworn Men of Meigate and the violent end of its leadership.

In year 49, the Covenant declared war on the Sworn Men of Meigate over a long-standing grievance. It defeated the Sworn Men at Meigate, killing 149, and continued to press the conflict. In year 50, the Covenant defeated the Sworn Men again at Meigate, killing 124, and took the settlement from them. The Sworn Men of Meigate was finished, its last 12 followers scattering. The Covenant’s internal stability broke when Keithfal Naell, its ruler, was killed by Tor Nathgoull at Vea Lode. Herpeim Raern took the seat of the Covenant by election in the same year.

The Covenant’s authority collapsed in year 51. Threi Cut rose against it, exploiting the fact that its standing had fallen to nothing. The Hadale Commune’s raid on Meigate was beaten off, but the Covenant could not hold its remaining territories. The war with the Sworn Men of Meigate ended in peace after two years, but the Covenant itself was left diminished, its power broken by the loss of its ruler and the subsequent uprising.

The political landscape of the Kebarrow Compact in the early years of the new millennium was defined by violent instability and shifting alliances. In Y0027, Teillmol Lund seized power through a coup, only to be expelled two years later after a failed assassination attempt on Thold Valmaer was traced back to him. His removal paved the way for Theald Va, whose own rule was cut short when he was murdered by Wilwound Ska in Hadale. Ska contested Beas Krouthea’s claim to the leadership and successfully overturned it, taking the seat for himself. However, Ska’s tenure was brief; he was assassinated at Kebarrow by Stonand Ker, leading to a contested election that Le Vild won against Kou Peis. Le Vild’s rule was marked by diplomatic marriages binding the Compact to the Griwick Compact and the Vea Lode Covenant, but also by war. The Griwick Compact declared war on the Kebarrow Compact, resulting in three years of conflict where the Compact and its allies repeatedly defeated Griwick forces at Kebarrow. Le Vild was eventually cast out after a failed attempt on Thold Valmaer, and Heth Fal took the seat. Heth Fal’s rule was equally turbulent, involving the murder of Thold Valmaer in Griwick and another failed attempt on Thurnean Kourn, which led to his own expulsion. Nael War succeeded him but was murdered by Neildvarn Tramern, a man who had previously been cast out for attempted murder. Paernrom Sir took the seat next but was also murdered, this time by Throll Kell, allowing Kondruth Tru to assume leadership. Kondruth Tru’s rule was ended by a coup led by Paernmel Has, who would hold power for over a decade. Paernmel Has faced numerous challenges, including several failed assassination attempts and uncovered conspiracies by Stonand Ker, Keithfal Naell, and Throll Kell, resulting in their expulsion or execution. He also orchestrated the murder of Veillpea Dourn and Thres Thrild. Despite these internal purges and a beaten-off raid on Threi Cut, Paernmel Has maintained control until Y0051, when he was murdered at Kebarrow by Wuldweald Valdrith. Wuldweald then contested Hehum Skul’s claim to the leadership and successfully took the seat, casting out Skul and ending the period of intense internal strife with a new, albeit violent, transfer of power.

The Kebarrow Compact’s grip on power in year 27 was shattered when Teillmol Lund openly challenged Gatros Hearn for the seat, seizing control through a coup that cast Hearn out. This instability was compounded by a failed raid on Griwick, which prompted Hadale to break away and form the Hadale Commune. Lund’s tenure was short-lived; after a traced attempt on Thold Valmaer failed, he was expelled for attempted murder, allowing Theald Va to take the seat via election. However, the Compact’s internal rot continued as Tor Nathgoull was also cast out for a failed attempt on Va, who was subsequently murdered by Wilwound Ska at Hadale. Ska contested Beas Krouthea’s claim and won, but his rule ended when he was murdered by Stonand Ker at Kebarrow. Le Vild then seized the seat from Kou Peis, binding the Compact to Griwick through marriage, only for Griwick to declare war. The Compact, bolstered by allies, defeated Griwick at Kebarrow in a series of bloody engagements that lasted three years. During this conflict, Le Vild was cast out for another failed attempt on Valmaer, and Heth Fal took the seat. Heth Fal’s reign was marked by the murder of Thold Valmaer at Griwick and further defeats against Griwick, before peace was finally made. Heth Fal himself was cast out for attempting to kill Thurnean Kourn, and Nael War took the seat, only to be murdered by Neildvarn Tramern. Paernrom Sir then won the contested seat from Herpeim Raern, but was quickly murdered by Throll Kell, allowing Kondruth Tru to take power. Kondruth Tru’s rule was cut short by a coup from Paernmel Has, who managed to survive multiple assassination attempts and uncovered conspiracies from Stonand Ker, Keithfal Naell, and Throll Kell. Paernmel Has expanded the Compact’s influence through marriages to the Sworn Men of Laehiford and the Hadale Commune, but his long rule ended when he was murdered by Wuldweald Valdrith at Kebarrow. Valdrith then contested Hehum Skul’s claim and successfully took the seat, casting Skul out and securing his own position as ruler.

In 22, the Griwick Compact’s raid on Hadale was beaten off. By 23, the Kebarrow Compact bound itself to the Sworn Men of Meigate through the marriage of Saern Meastouth and Renbeir Surn, and to the Sworn Men of Laehiford through the marriage of Tor Nathgoull and Realsis Leirpu. That same year, Saern Meastouth challenged Weallhous Dreld openly for the Kebarrow Compact and was beaten. Weallhous Dreld then killed Saern Meastouth at Kebarrow. The Sworn Men of Meigate raided Hadale, carrying off grain and killing twelve, while the Sworn Men of Laehiford raided Kebarrow, carrying off grain and killing twenty-three.

In 25, Sothkel Sald married Leimmil Theall, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Griwick Compact. Gatros Hearn challenged Weallhous Dreld openly for the Kebarrow Compact and took the seat, executing a coup. Weallhous Dreld was killed by Gatros Hearn at Kebarrow. Gatros Hearn then had Leimmil Theall murdered at Griwick. In 26, Stonand Ker married Kreathbeas Waeth, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Sworn Men of Meigate. The Kebarrow Compact’s raid on Threi Cut was beaten off.

In 27, Sothkel Sald’s attempt on Gatros Hearn failed and was traced back to the earlier grievance. Sothkel Sald was cast out. Teillmol Lund challenged Gatros Hearn openly for the Kebarrow Compact and took the seat, executing a coup. Gatros Hearn was cast out. The Kebarrow Compact’s raid on Griwick was beaten off, leading Hadale to break from the Kebarrow Compact as the Hadale Commune. Teillmol Lund’s attempt on Thold Valmaer failed, and he was cast out. Theald Va took the seat by election. Tor Nathgoull’s attempt on Theald Va failed, and he was cast out. Wilwound Ska murdered Theald Va at Hadale.

Wilwound Ska contested Beas Krouthea’s claim to the Kebarrow Compact, overturning it and taking the seat. Beas Krouthea was cast out. In 30, Neildvarn Tramern married Thurnean Kourn, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Griwick Compact. In 31, Stonand Ker murdered Wilwound Ska at Kebarrow. Le Vild contested Kou Peis’s claim, overturning it and taking the seat. Kou Peis was cast out. Le Vild married Tharhith Beamma, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Griwick Compact. Paernmel Has married Stald Gearngoll, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Vea Lode Covenant.

In 32, the Griwick Compact declared war on the Kebarrow Compact. The Kebarrow Compact and its allies defeated the Griwick Compact at Kebarrow. Le Vild’s attempt on Thold Valmaer failed, and he was cast out. The Kebarrow Compact and its allies defeated the Griwick Compact at Kebarrow again. Heth Fal contested Drarka Draernthun’s claim, overturning it and taking the seat. Drarka Draernthun was cast out. Heth Fal murdered Thold Valmaer at Griwick. The Kebarrow Compact and its allies defeated the Griwick Compact at Kebarrow again.

In 35, Kondruth Tru married Durnrin Drar, binding the Kebarrow Compact to the Hadale Commune.

The Kebarrow Compact endured twenty years of internal fragmentation and external hostility, defined by a succession of eleven rulers who each held the seat for an average of 1.7 years. The period began with the Compact bound to the Sworn Men of Meigate and the Sworn Men of Laehiford through marriage, but these alliances were quickly tested by raids and open challenges. The rule of Weallhous Dreld ended when he was killed by Gatros Hearn after losing an open challenge, initiating a cycle of violence where the seat passed ten times. The Compact suffered three raids in its early years and launched two raids that were both beaten off, while simultaneously losing the settlement of Hadale to the Hadale Commune.

A war with the Griwick Compact began in year 32 over a long-standing grievance and lasted three years. The Kebarrow Compact and its allies defeated the Griwick Compact at Kebarrow in years 32, 33, and 34, with 103, 121, and 60 dead respectively. The conflict ended in year 35 with peace declared, leaving both sides exhausted. During this time, the Compact ordered two killings against people of other powers: Leimmil Theall at Griwick in year 25 and Thold Valmaer at Griwick in year 34. The internal stability of the Compact remained poor, with twelve people cast out and six of its own people murdered from within.

The period concluded with Paernmel Has holding the seat after taking it in year 39. The rule of Kondruth Tru had ended when Paernmel Has won an open challenge, casting out Kondruth Tru. Throughout the twenty years, twenty people were courted away from the ruler, indicating a persistent pattern of disloyalty. The Kebarrow Compact emerged from the period with its seat held by a new ruler, having survived the war with the Griwick Compact but retaining the scars of frequent leadership changes and the loss of Hadale.

Paernmel Has took the seat in year 39 and held it at the end of the period, but the Compact remained a fragile entity, having survived a war it won but losing territory and enduring constant leadership turnover.

The Kebarrow Compact endured twenty years of internal fragmentation and external hostility, defined by a succession of eleven rulers who held the seat for an average of 1.7 years each. The period began with Weallhous Dreld holding power, bound by marriage to the Sworn Men of Meigate and the Sworn Men of Laehiford, but ended with Paernmel Has still in the seat after a decade of violent turnover. The Compact’s stability was undermined by a pattern of twenty individuals being courted away from its ruler, a structural decay that facilitated frequent purges and contested successions. While the Compact fought three wars against the Griwick Compact, winning all three battles at Kebarrow, it suffered the loss of Hadale to the Hadale Commune and endured two raids that carried off plunder.

The early years were marked by the consolidation of alliances and the violent removal of challengers. Weallhous Dreld kept the seat after defeating Saern Meastouth’s open challenge in 23, but was himself killed by Gatros Hearn in 25 after losing an open challenge. Gatros Hearn’s rule was brief; he was cast out after losing a subsequent challenge to Teillmol Lund in 27. Teillmol Lund was also cast out in 28 for attempted murder, leading to the election of Theald Va. Theald Va was murdered in 29 by Wilwound Ska, who then took the seat by setting aside the claim of the named heir Beas Krouthea. Wilwound Ska was killed in 31 by Stonand Ker, who had been motivated by the earlier raid on Threi Cut. The Sworn Men of Meigate emerged in 19 when Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact. Internal stability was fragile; Sou Dra returned from exile in 20 to serve the group but was cast out after losing a coup against Renbeir Surn in 22. Renbeir ruled until his death in 25, at which point Kreathbeas Waeth took the seat as no claimant remained. The new leadership faced immediate hardship, with a famine in 26 causing 64 deaths and a grain shortage.

Kreathbeas Waeth’s tenure was marked by failed military expeditions and internal conspiracy. Raids on Griwick, Vea Lode, and Threi Cut were beaten off between 28 and 31. In 39, Gatros Hearn began conspiring against the ruler, an attempt that failed in 41 but led to Hearn’s expulsion after his plot was uncovered a year later. The faction suffered further during famines in 42 and 43, with the latter causing 75 deaths and widespread abandonment of Meigate. In response to external pressure from the Vea Lode Covenant, which raided Meigate in 43, Treild Haen married Stoulthoth Frorn in 47, binding the Sworn Men of Meigate to the Sworn Men of Laehiford.

Kreathbeas Waeth died in 48, and Herpeim Raern took the seat through election. His rule was short-lived; he was challenged by Treild Haen in 50 and cast out following a coup. Treild Haen’s own leadership ended quickly when an attempt on Viskeil Von failed in 51, leading to his expulsion for attempted murder. Beas Krouthea took the seat through election in 51, concluding the period with the faction having survived internal purges and external raids but remaining vulnerable to famine and shifting alliances.

The reign of Le Vild over the Kebarrow Compact began in turmoil, marked by his violent seizure of power from Kou Peis in Y0031 and the subsequent exile of his rival. His rule was cemented through strategic marriages that bound the Compact to the Griwick and Vea Lode factions, yet these alliances could not shield him from the conspiracies brewing within his own ranks. Thosruld Lul’s early plots were followed by a devastating war with the Griwick Compact, which the Kebarrow forces managed to repel at their capital in Y0032, though the conflict dragged on for years. Le Vild’s paranoia led him to attempt the murder of Thold Valmaer, an act that backfired spectacularly and resulted in his own expulsion from the Compact he had ruled. Heth Fal succeeded him, but his tenure was equally bloody; he orchestrated the assassination of Thold Valmaer before attempting to kill Thurnean Kourn, a failure that cost him his seat. Nael War took power next, only to be assassinated by Neildvarn Tramern after years of simmering resentment among the nobility. Paernrom Sir briefly held the throne but was murdered in Hadale by Throll Kell, allowing Kondruth Tru to take office through election. However, stability remained elusive as Paernmel Has staged a coup against Tru, seizing the seat and initiating a long period of internal purges. For nearly two decades, Paernmel Has ruled while systematically rooting out conspirators like Stonand Ker, Keithfal Naell, and Throll Kell, executing some and exiling others after their plots were uncovered. He also engaged in external violence, murdering Veillpea Dourn and Thres Thrild to settle old scores. Despite binding the Compact to new allies through marriage, his reign ended when Wuldweald Valdrith uncovered a conspiracy stemming from earlier raids and assassinated Paernmel Has at Kebarrow. In the ensuing power vacuum, Wuldweald contested Hehum Skul’s claim, successfully overturning it to take the seat for himself, casting out Skul and continuing the cycle of violent succession that defined the era.

The Griwick Compact ended its rule in 36, having lost its seat, its land, and its standing. The period began with a violent succession in 24, when Thold Valmaer killed Turaer Danpa and Leimmil Theall took the seat by the strongest claim. Thold Valmaer took the seat in 25 after Leimmil Theall was killed, but his rule was short-lived. The Compact’s standing fell to nothing as Threi Cut rose against it in 31. Thold Valmaer was killed in 34, and Thurnean Kourn took the seat after contesting Veillpea Dourn’s claim. Veillpea Dourn was cast out.

The Griwick Compact made peace with the Kebarrow Compact in 35 after three years of war. However, the Vea Lode Covenant took Griwick from the Griwick Compact in 35. The Griwick Compact was finished, its last six followers scattering. The Vea Lode Covenant and the Griwick Compact made peace in 36, but the Compact no longer existed as a ruling power.

The end of the Griwick Compact was marked by war and territorial loss. Thold Valmaer was killed by Heth Fal at Griwick in year 34, and Thurnean Kourn took the seat after his claim was upheld. The Griwick Compact’s rule from 24 to 36 was defined by rapid succession, internal decay, and total destruction. The Compact faced ten raids and five battles, losing all five. The Compact’s decline was marked by plague and war. A plague broke out at Griwick in 26, killing 185 people. In 27, 133 died and 296 fled. In 28, 156 died and 208 fled. The Kebarrow Compact’s rule over ten years was defined by the violent consolidation of Paernmel Has’s authority and the subsequent collapse of that order. At the start of the period, Has held the seat, having succeeded in 39. His tenure was marked by a series of internal challenges that were met with expulsion and execution, followed by external raids that failed to secure territory. The period ended with the murder of Has and the seizure of the seat by Wuldweald Valdrith, who displaced the previous heir through a contested election.

Has’s grip on power was secured through the removal of five rivals who attempted his life. In 43, Stonand Ker was cast out after an attempt on Has failed. Later that year, Keithfal Naell was cast out for a similar failed attempt. In 46, Throll Kell was cast out after his attempt failed. These expulsions were followed by the uncovering of conspiracies: Ker was declared outlaw, Naell was put to death, and Kell was declared outlaw. In 49, Drouldthas Stour was cast out after his attempt failed. During this time, Has ordered two killings of people from other powers, having Veillpea Dourn murdered at Vea Lode in 46 and Thres Thrild murdered at Griwick in 47.

The Compact’s external posture was uniformly unsuccessful. It sent out three raids, all of which were beaten off. A raid on Vea Lode in 43, a raid on Threi Cut in 48, and a raid on Griwick in 49 all failed to carry off plunder. Internally, the Compact suffered one murder from within its own people, a purge in which Paernmel Has was killed at Kebarrow in 51 by Wuldweald Valdrith. This act triggered a contest for the seat. Valdrith contested Hehum Skul’s claim in an election. Valdrith’s claim was upheld, and he took the seat. Skul was cast out for the losing claim.

The Sworn Men of Meigate spent thirty-three years defined by internal fracture and external failure. External relations deteriorated into a series of repelled attacks. Raids on Griwick, Vea Lode, and Threi Cut were all beaten off, with the Vea Lode Covenant retaliating by raiding Meigate in year 43. Leadership shifted again after Kreathbeas Waeth died in year 48; Herpeim Raern took the seat by election but was challenged and cast out by Treild Haen in year 50. Treild Haen’s own rule ended when he attempted murder and was cast out, allowing Beas Krouthea to take the seat by election in year 51.

The Sworn Men of Meigate began in year 19 as a breakaway from the Kebarrow Compact, establishing independence at Meigate. Over the 33 years, five people held the seat: two died, one was replaced, one was cast out, and one was still holding. Eight raids were sent out, six beaten off and two carrying plunder. In 19, Meigate broke from the Kebarrow Compact to form the Sworn Men of Meigate. In 20, Sou Dra returned from exile and took service with the new power. The Griwick Compact’s twenty-year rule, spanning years 4 to 23, was defined by a cycle of external aggression and internal collapse. The Compact’s standing fell to nothing, leading to uprisings at Vea Lode in year 15 and Threi Cut in year 15. Within the seat, three people were murdered by their own: Pouldrir Ho was killed by Math Ham in year 20, Heillvar Maer was killed by Turaer Danpa in year 21, and Befu Seirn was killed by Bu Rumpirn in year 23. The seat passed from one person to another three times. Pouldrir Ho, who had held the seat since year 1, was killed. Heillvar Maer took the seat in year 20 after his claim was upheld against Math Ham, and was killed. Befu Seirn took the seat in year 21 by the strongest claim and was killed.
